facts.fact: HMIS Eswatini's Q1 2026 account says in-country developers completed OpenFn training, with automated FHIR-aligned data flows from the CMIS SQL Server environment into DHIS2 as the outcome.

Jembi says healthcare facilities in Eswatini can now share demographic and clinical patient information in near real-time through a FHIR-based exchange on the OpenHIM Platform, with a Master Patient Index integrated; no facility count is given.
facts.system: OpenHIM Platform / FHIR-based health information exchange with Master Patient Index

note: as_of is the published date (year inferred by the source's own note); no go-live date is given. Scaling to more facilities is listed as a next step, so no breadth fact; the Population Registry is used for patient identification but is not stated to be the national ID, so no identifier fact.

facts.fact: The Digital Landscape Assessment Report, as reported by Independent News, describes the Ministry of Health's Health Information Exchange system, based on HL7/FHIR integration standards, as the most technically advanced architecture observed in the assessment of 21 ministries; no systems it links are named (date is the story's published date).

HMIS Eswatini says a workshop validated the CMIS-eLMIS integration for ART medicines (dispensing in CMIS updates eLMIS stock), working and ready for pilot at facility level with national scale-up in view; as_of is the publication date, the document says only 'recent'.

note: Describes CMIS as a single EMR with cloud backup so records follow the patient; no exchange between health systems or national identifier linkage is stated.
Passages hold only the cover, contents and acronym list; DHIS2 is named in the acronyms with no description and nothing on exchange.
Excerpt stops before the HMIS chapter; CMIS appears only in the acronym list and the HRIS description concerns staff data, so nothing on health-system exchange.

facts.fact: The US State Department report says Eswatini's CMIS works through its own data capture as well as interoperability with other relevant systems, and over 90 percent of HIV commodity consumption data is sourced from it.

note: No exchange between health systems stated.

facts.fact: Eswatini's Ministry of Health launched the National Health Intelligence Platform on 16 November 2026, which the minister said will bring clinical, epidemiological, supply-chain and community data into one integrated system.
